name: In-Country Refugee or Protected Person Claim

qualifying_event.description: Any person already in New Zealand (including on a temporary visa) who fears persecution in their home country may lodge an in-country claim for refugee or protected person status: a Confirmation of Claim form (INZ 1071) with identity evidence, a written statement, an interview with a Refugee and Protection Officer, a claim report, final submissions, and a decision. Current wait time from lodging to allocation to an officer is reported at 18-24 months.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: INZ 1071 Confirmation of Claim form; passport/identity evidence; written statement of claim; interview attendance; supporting persecution/risk evidence where available.

requirements.blocker_text: Must meet the 1951 Refugee Convention definition. Around one-fifth of refugee and protection claims made are currently successful.

Convention Against Torture / ICCPR-based protected-person grounds, for claimants who do not meet the refugee definition; excluded if previously rejected on specified Immigration Act 2009 grounds (e.g. s137(2) serious-acts exclusion).

evidence_required.document: INZ 1071 Confirmation of Claim form and identity evidence
Written statement of claim (per INZ 1362 guidelines)

outcome.duration_length: Successful claimants may apply for a Permanent Resident Visa on the basis of the recognition

sources.title: Immigration New Zealand -- Claiming refugee or protected person status: 6-step in-country process, 18-24 month wait to RPO allocation, ~1-in-5 success rate
Immigration New Zealand Operations Manual -- successful refugee/protected person claimants may apply for a Permanent Resident Visa on the basis of that recognition, subject to exclusion grounds

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (New Zealand). work_rights and study_rights modeled 'restricted' to reflect conditions during the (often 18-24+ month) wait and assessment period before a decision, in contrast to nz_refugee_quota_programme.json's immediate full-rights Permanent Residence on arrival. The claimed-outcome source (opsmanual/43643.htm) displayed an archival caveat in the fetch but its stated outcome (direct eligibility for a Permanent Resident Visa) is treated as reliable since it aligns with the parallel quota-programme outcome and no contradicting current-policy source was found. The reported roughly 20% success rate is disclosed as a real-world caveat, not modeled as a formal selection_odds figure since it is not a quota-style allocation.
